correctness.rationale: PASS because Legendre's exact exclusion set yields an open 2-adic obstruction whose closure adds only zero, and integer preservation equals inverse-image inclusion. For odd slopes Haar-measure invariance forces zero intercept, and multiplication then requires slope congruent to one modulo eight. For slopes of exact 2-adic valuation one, a measure defect (odd intercept) or a residue contradiction (even intercept) rules out preservation. Common factors of four reduce the remaining cases to the explicitly safe and unsafe residues modulo eight. Disjoint recursion counts all positive affine maps and gives 3/20 density. Exact direct triple-sum enumeration, 16512 slope–intercept pairs, and box recurrence checks corroborate the unrestricted proof.
